name: Control Precision
definition: The ability to quickly and repeatedly adjust the controls of a machine or a vehicle to exact positions.

benchmark.name: CARLA Leaderboard
benchmark.model_or_system: World on Rails (Rails), Chen & Koltun, UT Austin / Intel Labs
benchmark.metric: CARLA Leaderboard 1.0 Driving Score (0-100, route completion × infraction penalty), SENSORS track
benchmark.human_reference: Licensed adult drivers / vehicle operators (general driving workforce)

benchmark.name: CARLA Leaderboard
benchmark.metric: Driving Score (0-100 composite: route completion × infraction penalty)
benchmark.human_reference: Licensed adult drivers, the typical person who operates vehicle controls at work (e.g., delivery or commercial drivers), driving the same simulated routes with standard controls.

benchmark.name: CARLA Leaderboard 2.0
benchmark.metric: Driving Score (0-100 scale; route completion % multiplied by infraction penalty)
benchmark.human_reference: Licensed adult drivers, the typical workforce member who operates vehicles as part of work (e.g., delivery or professional drivers), driving in a simulator.

benchmark.name: A2RL Drone Championship
benchmark.model_or_system: TU Delft MAVLab autonomous drone (G&CNet direct motor-control policy)
benchmark.metric: seconds to complete two laps of the 170 m course (lower is better)
benchmark.human_reference: Specialist workforce: professional and commercial drone/UAV operators and FPV pilots. These are the people who would perform fine, rapid manual control of a drone in work settings.

benchmark.name: A2RL Drone Championship
benchmark.model_or_system: TII Racing autonomous drone (Technology Innovation Institute)
benchmark.metric: seconds (fastest autonomous lap time, lower is better)
benchmark.human_reference: Specialist workforce: people who fly drones or FPV aircraft in work settings (commercial and professional drone operators, including professional racing pilots), with the median operator as the reference point.
